messages.content: Extract source facts about return/destruction duties and permission/prohibition to retain information after that process. Read only effects asserted by the focus; other units are context. Copy actor, recipient, requester and restriction phrases verbatim from cited source units. Different effects keep their own actors. Do not fill every possible category: empty lists are correct if no such effect is asserted. A heading, information definition, signature copy or postal return receipt is not a disposal/retention norm. Do not invent a duty, destruction option, termination trigger, retained-copy prohibition, or actor. information_scope identifies the exact semantic scope, not a keyword match: confidential_information; copies_of_confidential_information; confidential_information_and_copies; copies_and_derivatives; derivatives. For each duty give its action, actual return recipient, alternative triggers, and explicit exceptions. requester_phrase is used only for a request trigger. retention_exception_indices links that duty to actual permission records in post_disposal_retention, numbered from0. Empty exceptions assert that no exception limits this duty; if unresolved, omit the duty and explain instead. For a retention permission, restriction_phrase must retain ALL stated quantity, purpose, location and legal conditions, using an exact continuous source phrase; source_scoped means that phrase is supplied, none means no additional condition. A prohibition is not an exception or permission. State whether the retention effect applies after return/destruction. If the supplied fields cannot express an effect faithfully, put the issue in unresolved, do not force a category. These are current-source facts, not answers to a legal test question. Cite a focus unit in every record. Return only the response schema.

{"focus_unit_ids":[58],"current_source_units":[{"id":58,"text":"Upon the Disclosing Party’s request, the Receiving Party will promptly return to the Disclosing Party all materials or tangible items containing the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information and all copies thereof; provided, however, Receiving Party’s legal department or outside legal counsel may maintain a single copy of Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information for purposes of regulatory compliance and compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement."}]}
